reasoning.text:
[Before action · inspect]
Identify all interactive-looking objects, the grid geometry, and any text or symbols in the initial puzzle.

[Before action · pixels]
Map exact occupied 8x8 grid cells for the lower-left purple launcher, white cross, trajectory, blue cluster, and top purple piece.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Tentative game model:
- Main playfield is an 8 px grid. A purple piece near an edge is the current projectile; the same purple shape in the dark top tray may be the next/held piece.
- A blue cluster is the receiver. Its gray interior/aperture matches the projectile shape.
- Gray dotted cells form the projected straight trajectory from the projectile center through a white crosshair. ACTION6 likely aims/fires; choose a click collinear with projectile center and aperture center (clicking the aperture center is safest).
- Progress total is 9, plausibly nine one-shot placements. Re-evaluate after the first click; ACTION7 is undo.

[Before action · message]
I expect a click at the gray aperture’s center to fire the 3×3 purple piece along the shown diagonal, fill the opening, and advance progress to 1/9.

[Before action · message]
The board returned to its starting arrangement and progress stayed 0/9; the five frames imply an attempted motion failed or reset. I’ll inspect that animation before spending another action.

[Before action · inspect]
What moved during the first click, along what path, and where/why did it fail? Compare all archived action frames.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Game model (visual-search matching):
- The dark gridded header (y=0..79) shows the current target glyph, including its exact color and occupied 8×8 cells.
- Click the identical glyph somewhere in the black playfield (y=80..503). Other colored structures, gray trails, and white glyphs are distractors.
- A click creates a brief white pulse at that coordinate. A wrong click leaves progress unchanged and shortens the segmented white bottom bar by 16 px; avoid guessing. ACTION7 exists but is unnecessary unless explicitly useful.
- Each correct match should advance one of 9 rounds and redraw a new target/field. Use exact shape/color matching and click near the glyph center.

[Before action · message]
The only exact copy of the header’s purple 3×3 target is the purple 3×3 block at bottom-left. I expect clicking its center to advance to the second of nine searches.

[Before action · message]
Both colored endpoints ignored direct clicks, while the white plus is the only distinct active object on their dotted route. I expect clicking its center to register the first hit/collection and redraw the scene; if not, the pulse mechanic itself will clarify the needed interaction.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Revised movement model:
- Header shows the controlled purple piece (currently a filled 3×3 block), not a visual-search query.
- In the playfield, the purple piece travels toward a blue receiver whose gray aperture matches it. Gray cells mark the route.
- A white glyph on the route is a mandatory waypoint/collectible. Clicking it teleports/moves the purple piece onto it and removes the white glyph; direct clicks on the receiver are ignored while such a waypoint remains.
- After collecting the mandatory white waypoint, click the center of the receiver’s gray aperture; likely completes a stage. Clicking the piece itself does nothing.
- Bottom segmented bar loses 16 px per action, so use only required waypoint(s), then receiver. Progress total is 9.

[Before action · message]
The waypoint vanished and the purple block now occupies its center; the route to the gray aperture is clear. I expect clicking the aperture center now to deliver the block and advance progress.

[Before action · message]
The receiver is still too far to select directly. I’ll inspect the successful waypoint action’s intermediate frames to determine whether movement is stepwise and what range/order it enforces.

[Before action · inspect]
During the successful click on the white waypoint, did the purple block travel, swap, grow, or get recreated? Track both its old and new positions across all frames.

[Before action · message]
The successful animation shows an imploding white pulse pulling the nearby purple block to the click center. Its first displacement was 48 cells-pixels per axis; I’ll repeat that safe maximum-style diagonal step at (132,380), expecting the block to relocate there.

[Before action · message]
The block moved exactly to (132,380), confirming the pulse-pull model. I’ll continue on the dotted diagonal with another known-safe 48-by-48 step to (180,332).

[Before action · message]
The block again advanced to the intended center with no deviation. Next I expect the same pull to place it at (228,284).

[Before action · message]
The block is now centered at (228,284), still exactly on the guide. The next safe pulse should move it to (276,236).

[Before action · message]
The block reached (276,236). One more full safe step to (324,188) should leave it within a final short pull of the receiver.

[Before action · message]
The piece is at (324,188). To avoid parking it on the blue rim, I’ll use the last gray guide cell just outside the receiver at (340,172); from there the aperture is exactly one proven-safe 48-by-48 pull away.

[Before action · message]
The block now sits cleanly at (340,172), and the matching 3×3 gray aperture is one safe pulse away. I expect clicking (388,124) to seat the block and register the objective.

[Before action · message]
The purple block was pulled into the aperture, progress advanced to 1/9, and the bar reset. The new board has a yellow 4×4 header glyph, a solid blue disk, and scattered cyan cells; I’ll map these before acting.

[Before action · inspect]
Map the second level: identify exact header glyphs, all playfield objects/cells, their centers, shapes, colors, and any implied route or matching aperture.

[Before action · inspect]
Across the level-transition frames, when and how do the yellow header block, blue disk, and cyan playfield cells appear; is any yellow player piece present before the final frame?

[Before action · inspect]
How does the purple piece interact with the blue receiver in the successful final pull, and does the header/palette react before the next level?

[Before action · pixels]
Give the exact 8×8-grid occupancy/color map of level 2's playfield and header, to reveal symmetry or hidden shapes.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Confirmed core mechanics:
- ACTION6 creates a white imploding pulse centered on the clicked 8×8-grid cell. A movable connected piece is pulled to that center when any part is within the pulse's roughly 64 px radius. The segmented bottom bar loses 16 px per click and resets at each level (32-click budget).
- Level 1: header showed the movable purple 3×3 block. Pull it along the gray route into the matching 3×3 gray aperture of the fixed blue receiver. A 48 px change in x and y (67.9 px center distance) is confirmed safe; clicking too far does nothing. Final aperture insertion advances progress.
- Receiver blue structures do not move under ordinary pulses (at least in level 1). White/gray/cyan single cells may be guides or collectibles; do not assume they themselves are the player.
- Progress is 9 levels. Each new level can introduce UI/mechanics; re-identify the movable piece, receiver/aperture, guides, and palette before acting.

[Before action · write WORKING.md]
Progress 1/9, level 2 at turn 11 frame 13. Header: black palette box with four 2×2 swatches centered (16,16) cyan, (48,16) magenta, (80,16) purple, (112,16) yellow; separate yellow 4×4 glyph centered (256,40). Playfield: fixed-looking solid blue 69-cell disk centered (268,220), radius ~40. Eight cyan 1-cell markers centered at (148,300),(332,300),(300,324),(132,332),(396,436),(116,444),(380,452),(132,460). Bottom click budget full. No visible yellow movable piece or blue aperture. Need infer whether palette spawns/selects a piece, cyan markers guide movement, or blue disk must be altered.

[Before action · message]
The nearest cyan marker at (332,300) lies just within one pulse’s reach of the blue disk’s lower-right edge. I’ll click it: if the disk is the movable body, it should be pulled onto and consume that marker; otherwise the unchanged scene will rule out that route model.

[Before action · message]
The blue disk did not move. Instead, the clicked cyan 1-cell seed became a magenta 2×2 block, matching the header’s color-order legend. I’ll inspect the five frames to determine whether this is growth, palette cycling, or a spawned piece.

[Before action · inspect]
Track the clicked cyan seed and new magenta 2×2 block across turn 12 frames: does the cyan cell grow/recolor in place, move, or combine with something from the header? Does any header glyph change?

[Before action · write WORKING.md]
Progress 1/9, level 2. Exact initial objects in prior working state. Turn12 clicked cyan seed (332,300): blue disk stayed fixed; after shrink-pulse the seed transformed in place into a magenta 2×2 block occupying x320..335,y288..303. Header legend order is cyan→magenta→purple→yellow and target preview is yellow 4×4, strongly suggesting repeated direct clicks grow/recolor one seed: 1×1 cyan -> 2×2 magenta -> 3×3 purple -> 4×4 yellow. Next test: click inside same block at original anchor (332,300), expect purple3×3.

[Before action · message]
The header legend matches a size/color evolution: cyan seed → magenta 2×2 → purple 3×3 → yellow 4×4 target. I expect a second click on the evolved block at (332,300) to produce the purple 3×3 tier.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Confirmed core mechanics:
- ACTION6 creates a white imploding pulse centered on the click. Movable pieces intersecting the roughly 64 px pulse are pulled to its center; fixed blue structures stay put. Bottom segmented bar loses 16 px/click and resets per level (32-click budget).
- Level 1 was delivery: pull a purple 3×3 along guides into the blue receiver's matching gray aperture. A (+/−48,+/−48) displacement is safe; too-far clicks do nothing.
- Merge/growth levels: the header legend gives tier order cyan 1×1 seed → magenta 2×2 → purple 3×3 → yellow 4×4. A pulse that gathers TWO same-tier pieces at its center merges/upgrades them. Clicking a lone piece does nothing. Eight cyan seeds therefore need the 7 merges of a binary tree to make one yellow target. Choose pulse centers in the intersection of both pieces' capture ranges, biased toward where the next merge must occur. Larger pieces can be captured from farther center distances because their edges intersect the pulse.
- Progress is 9 levels; mechanics can vary. Header's large glyph is the current target tier/shape.

[Before action · message]
The second click on the lone magenta block did nothing, confirming that upgrades require pairing rather than repeated clicks. I’ll gather the top-left cyan pair at a right-biased center, (192,316), expecting a second magenta block positioned close enough to merge with the first.

[Before action · message]
Only the nearer cyan seed moved to the snapped grid center (196,316); the seed at (132,332) was just outside capture range. They are now 66 px apart, so a pulse at (188,324) should catch both and merge them while keeping the result right-biased.

[Before action · message]
The cyan pair merged into a magenta 2×2 centered about (184,320). Its 146 px separation from the other magenta exceeds their combined capture reach, so I’ll first pull only the left block to (228,316), expecting no tier change but a much shorter gap.

[Before action · message]
The left magenta relocated to center (224,312); it is now only about 105 px from the right magenta at (328,296). A midpoint pulse at (276,308) should gather both and upgrade them to one purple 3×3.

[Before action · message]
The two top magentas merged successfully into a purple 3×3 centered at (276,308). I’ll now gather the bottom-left cyan pair at a right-biased but safely reachable center, (172,452), to form a magenta near the middle.

[Before action · message]
The bottom-left pair became a magenta centered at (168,448). Symmetrically, a pulse at (340,444) should gather the two bottom-right cyan seeds into the second magenta.

[Before action · message]
Both bottom pairs are now magenta, centered roughly at (168,448) and (336,440), too far to merge directly. I’ll pull only the left block to (220,444), reducing their separation to about 120 px.

[Before action · message]
The left magenta relocated to (216,440); the pair is now 120 px apart. A midpoint pulse at (276,440) should capture both edges and upgrade them to the second purple 3×3.

[Before action · message]
The lower pair merged into a purple 3×3; the two purples are 136 px apart. Before risking a one-pulse final merge at the edge of capture range, I’ll measure whether clicks snap to grid centers and the effective pulse center from prior frames.

[Before action · inspect]
For turn 14's click at (192,316), locate the exact implosion center relative to the 8px grid and show the nearer moved cyan seed and farther unmoved seed; determine whether the pulse centered at x=192 or snapped to cell center 196.

[Before action · message]
The purple centers are (276,308) and about (276,444). Because pulse centers land on grid cells, no single midpoint puts an outer cell of both within the ~60 px capture radius. I’ll pull only the lower purple upward to (276,412), after which both will be safely reachable.

[Before action · message]
The lower purple is now centered at (276,412), only 104 px below the upper one. A midpoint pulse at (276,360) should merge both into the yellow 4×4 shown in the header and complete level 2.

[Before action · message]
The two purples did merge into the yellow 4×4, but progress did not advance, so the solid blue disk is the final sink. I’ll pull the yellow block upward to (268,292), within one subsequent pulse of the disk center.

[Before action · message]
The yellow block moved to center about (264,288), directly beneath the disk; its top cells are now 56 px from the disk center. Clicking (268,220) should pull it into the blue sink and complete the level.

[Before action · message]
The yellow block was absorbed by the blue disk, advancing progress to 2/9 and resetting the level. Level 3 now shows yellow 4×4 and purple 3×3 targets, several cyan/magenta ingredients, and two blue sinks; I’ll map all centers and counts before merging.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Confirmed core mechanics:
- ACTION6 makes an imploding pulse. Any movable connected piece with at least one occupied cell center within about 60 px of the click is pulled to the click's grid cell; fixed blue structures stay put. Bottom bar is a 32-click level budget.
- Same-tier pieces that land together merge upward: cyan 1×1 → magenta 2×2 → purple 3×3 → yellow 4×4. Clicking a lone piece at its current location does nothing. Use midpoint/biased pulses; grid-cell placement matters. For a piece of side n cells, outer cell centers extend 4(n−1) px from its geometric center along an axis, increasing capture reach.
- Header large glyph(s) show the final pieces required. After constructing each required piece, it must still be pulled into a solid blue disk/sink (or into a matching gray aperture when shown). Absorption advances the level only after all required deliveries.
- Level 1: delivered one existing purple 3×3 through guides into a blue aperture. Level 2: merged 8 cyan seeds into one yellow 4×4 (binary tree), then pulled it into a solid blue disk.
- New levels may require multiple target pieces/sinks; count ingredients and plan separate merge trees before acting.

[Before action · inspect]
Map level 3 exactly: list centers/sizes/colors of all header targets, cyan seeds, pre-merged magenta/purple pieces, and blue sinks; identify nearest natural pairings and sink centers.

[Before action · pixels]
Return exact 8×8-grid occupancy for level 3 so every movable piece and sink center can be computed.

[Before action · write WORKING.md]
Progress 2/9, level3 turn25 start. Header targets: yellow4 and purple3. Fixed blue sinks centers (76,404),(188,404). Movables: cyan seeds (252,124),(252,180),(100,188),(452,188),(492,188),(68,228); magenta2 centers (152,136),(376,184),(248,264). Seed-equivalent total12 = yellow8 + purple4.
Plan exploit cascades: click (204,152), within60 of both top cyans and a cell of magenta(152,136), hopefully cyan pair->magenta then both mags->purple in one action P1. Similarly click(436,188) gathers right cyan pair + magenta(376,184) to P2 purple (may cascade). Left: merge cyans (100,188)+(68,228) around(124,208); move output magenta toward ~176,228; merge with magenta(248,264) around208,252/260 ->P3. Merge P1+P3 ->yellow. Deliver right P2 to sink(188,404) in ~5 pulls; yellow to sink(76,404) in ~4. Re-evaluate exact output centers each step.

[Before action · message]
The top cyan pair and the existing magenta all intersect a pulse centered at (204,152). I expect one action to gather the two seeds into a magenta and immediately cascade that pair of magentas into a purple 3×3.

[Before action · message]
All three pieces returned to their starting positions and progress stayed unchanged; the 21-frame action signals a rejected mixed-tier collision rather than an ordinary miss. I’ll inspect key frames to see whether the cyan pair briefly merged before contact with the magenta.

[Before action · inspect]
During turn26's 21-frame three-piece pulse, which pieces moved/merged, what collision caused rejection, and when did they reset? Inspect representative frames.

[Before action · pixels]
Identify exact colors/cell arrangement at the pulse center during turn26 frames 4,8,12 to see which of the three inputs coexisted and whether cyan merged.

[Before action · write GUIDE.md]
Confirmed core mechanics:
- ACTION6 makes an imploding pulse. A movable connected piece is pulled if any occupied cell center is within about 60 px of the click; blue disks stay fixed. Bottom bar allows 32 clicks/level.
- Merge rule is strict: gather exactly two same-tier pieces at a pulse center to upgrade cyan1→magenta2→purple3→yellow4. Mixed-tier simultaneous capture makes a malformed mixed cluster, triggers a long rejection animation, and resets all involved pieces to their prior positions; recursive/cascade merging in one pulse does NOT work. Keep other tiers outside every merge pulse.
- Header large glyph(s) are required final pieces. After construction, pull each into a blue sink/aperture. Multiple targets require separate merge trees and deliveries.
- Plan using occupied-cell reach, not geometric center alone: pulse capture radius is ~60 px to any cell center; an n×n block's outer cell centers extend 4(n−1) px from its geometric center per axis.
- Level1 delivered existing purple3. Level2 merged 8 seeds to yellow4 and delivered it. Re-identify ingredients/targets each level.

[Before action · message]
The animation showed a rejected mixed 2×2 cluster: recursive merging is not allowed. I’ll first merge only the two top cyan seeds at their midpoint (252,152), keeping the existing magenta well outside the pulse.

[Before action · message]
The cyan pair became a magenta centered at (248,152), about 97 px from the original magenta at (152,136). A clean midpoint pulse at (200,144) should merge only those two into the first purple target piece.

[Before action · message]
The top pair merged into a purple centered at (204,148). I’ll now merge only the two rightmost cyan seeds at their midpoint, (472,188), safely away from the magenta at (376,184).

[Before action · message]
The right cyan pair became a magenta centered at (472,184), 96 px from the existing magenta at (376,184). A midpoint pulse at (424,184) should produce the second purple with no mixed-tier interference.

[Before action · message]
The right group is now a purple centered at (428,188). For the remaining merge tree, I’ll gather cyan seeds (100,188) and (68,228) at the far-right feasible center (124,208), producing a magenta biased toward the existing one at (248,264).

[Before action · message]
The cyan pair formed a magenta centered at (120,208). A pulse at (180,232) is just within reach of its lower-right cell but still outside the magenta at (248,264), so it should relocate only the new block closer.

[Before action · message]
The moved magenta is now centered at (176,232), only about 79 px from the existing magenta at (248,264). A midpoint pulse at (212,248) should merge just those two into the third purple.

[Before action · message]
The third purple is centered at (212,252), 104 px below the first at (204,148). A pulse at (208,200) lies well within an outer cell of both and should merge them into the required yellow 4×4, leaving the far-right purple untouched.

[Before action · write WORKING.md]
Level3 constructed required pieces: yellow4 centered(208,200), purple3 centered(428,188); fixed sinks(76,404),(188,404). Deliver yellow to left sink via pulse centers (168,248)->(128,296)->(88,344)->(76,404). Then purple to right sink via (380,236)->(332,284)->(284,332)->(236,380)->(188,404). Each planned displacement has an occupied cell center within 60. Avoid mixed collision; deliver yellow first so purple-route pulses cannot catch it.

[Before action · message]
The required yellow and purple pieces are built. I’ll deliver the yellow to the left sink first, beginning with a safe diagonal pull from (208,200) to (168,248).

[Before action · message]
The yellow block relocated exactly to (168,248). The next safe pull toward the left sink is (128,296).

[Before action · message]
The yellow is now at (128,296); pulling to (88,344) should place it immediately above the left blue disk.

[Before action · message]
The yellow block is directly above the left sink at (88,344), with an outer cell safely in range. Clicking the sink center (76,404) should absorb this first required piece while leaving the right purple untouched.

[Before action · message]
The yellow is now visibly locked inside the left disk; progress waits for the second delivery. I’ll start the purple’s five-pulse route to the right sink by moving it from (428,188) to (380,236).

[Before action · message]
The purple moved to (380,236). Next I expect a safe relocation to (332,284).

[Before action · message]
The purple is at (332,284); the next diagonal waypoint is (284,332).

[Before action · message]
The purple reached (284,332). Pulling it to (236,380) should park its left edge just outside the right sink, ready for the final insertion.

[Before action · message]
The purple is correctly parked at (236,380), adjacent to the right disk. Clicking its center (188,404) should lock the purple inside and complete both deliveries for level 3.

[Before action · message]
Both filled disks registered, advancing to 3/9. Level 4 has one yellow target, a single blue sink at bottom-left, scattered cyan seeds, and an irregular magenta cluster; I’ll map whether that cluster is one malformed object or several adjacent pieces before pulsing.

[Before action · inspect]
Map level 4 exactly: list all connected components, their cell patterns/centers/colors, sink center, and header target. Determine whether the pink cluster consists of separable magenta pieces or one irregular connected component.

[Before action · pixels]
Return exact level-4 grid/color map and distinguish the light-pink cluster's RGB from the magenta tier color in the palette.

[Before action · write WORKING.md]
Progress3/9 level4. Target yellow4; sink center(44,460). Fixed light-pink (#FF7BCC, not tier magenta) 8-cell decorative cluster near(436,168). Cyan seeds: (44,212),(92,212),(252,220),(292,236),(68,332),(100,380),(268,380),(244,412).
Plan four pairs. Bottom first: merge (68,332)+(100,380) at(120,356)->M3; merge(268,380)+(244,412) at(220,396)->M4; merge M3+M4 at(176,348)->P2. Top: merge(44,212)+(92,212) at(96,236)->M1; merge(252,220)+(292,236) at(236,244)->M2; move M1 to(148,252); merge M1+M2 at(188,272)->P1 (keeps P2 >60 from this mixed-tier pulse). Merge P1+P2 around(184,312) ->yellow. Deliver to sink via approx(132,364),(84,412),(44,460), adjusting from observed center.

[Before action · message]
There are exactly eight cyan seeds; the light-pink cluster is a separate fixed decoration. I’ll start the lower merge tree by gathering seeds (68,332) and (100,380) at the right/up-biased center (120,356).

[Before action · message]
The first lower pair became a magenta centered at (120,352). I’ll form the second from seeds (268,380) and (244,412) with a left-biased pulse at (220,396).

[Before action · message]
The lower magentas are centered at (120,352) and (216,392). A pulse at (176,348) reaches an occupied cell of both and should merge them into the lower purple while avoiding all upper seeds.

[Before action · message]
The lower tree produced a purple centered at (180,348). I’ll now merge upper-left seeds (44,212) and (92,212) at (96,236), biasing their magenta toward the center.

[Before action · message]
The cyan pair did merge, but a moving light-pink hazard reached the two remaining seeds during the same turn: they vanished and the header/sink turned gray. I’ll inspect the nine frames to confirm whether this is a reversible failure/reset and how far the hazard advances per action.

[Before action · inspect]
Track the light-pink hazard, remaining cyan seeds, header, sink, and merge across all turn47 frames. Did the hazard destroy seeds and trigger failure, or are colors only temporarily masked?

[Before action · pixels]
At turn47 final frame, list exact remaining colored cells/components and RGBs; specifically whether cyan seeds (252,220),(292,236) still exist, where the pink hazard is, and which objects are gray.

[Before action · message]
The final pixel map confirms the hazard consumed seed (292,236), graying the objective; seed (252,220) remains, so the level is otherwise unsolvable. I’ll undo the last pulse, expecting the eaten seed and colored objective to return at the pre-collision hazard position.

[Before action · message]
Undo fully restored the seed and colored objective. The hazard is approaching from the right, so I’ll immediately pull threatened seeds (252,220) and (292,236) leftward to (236,244); both are in range and should merge before the hazard reaches them.

[Before action · message]
The endangered seeds merged into a magenta centered near (232,240), but the hazard is now only about 48 px to its right and will advance again. I’ll pull that magenta left/down to (172,260), moving it out of the hazard’s path and toward the future top-left magenta.

[Before action · message]
The magenta escaped to (168,256); the hazard remains about 80 px to its right. I’ll merge the last cyan pair at (96,236), then immediately combine the two magentas before the hazard closes in.

[Before action · message]
The two magentas are now at (96,232) and (168,256), while the hazard is still to their right. A midpoint pulse at (132,244) should merge them into the second purple and pull the material farther left before contact.

[Before action · message]
The rescued tree is now a purple centered at (132,244); the earlier purple remains at (180,348). A pulse at (156,296) reaches both while drawing them downward away from the left-moving hazard, and should create the yellow target.

[Before action · message]
The purples merged into a yellow 4×4 centered about (152,296). The hazard is partly overlapping its left edge but has not triggered failure; I’ll immediately pull the yellow down-left to (108,348), separating it vertically while advancing toward the sink.

[Before action · message]
The yellow moved to roughly (104,344); the pink pattern passed beneath it without changing the target, so it appears to be a moving occluder rather than a destructive piece. I’ll pull the yellow to (68,400), immediately above the sink.

[Before action · message]
The yellow is centered at (64,400), directly above the blue disk; the pink pattern has moved into the disk independently. Clicking the sink center (44,460) should absorb the yellow and complete level 4.

[Before action · message]
The yellow was absorbed and progress advanced to 4/9. Level 5 presents four magenta 2×2 pieces—exactly enough for one yellow—plus a blue sink at the top and moving pink/cyan decorations near the bottom; I’ll map centers for the shortest merge-and-delivery plan.

[Before action · pixels]
Map level 5 exact component centers/sizes/colors, especially four tier-magenta blocks, blue sink, cyan cells, and light-pink moving shapes.

[Before action · write WORKING.md]
Progress4/9 level5. Yellow target; solid blue sink center(268,124). Tier magenta centers: L1(56,208),L2(120,232),R1(344,216),R2(448,216). Light-pink shapes/cyan cells lower field are moving decor/occluders.
Efficient plan: merge left mags at(116,232)->P1; merge right at(388,216)->P2. Move P1 to(184,232) and P2 to(320,216), using outer purple cells at exactly ~60 px. Merge at(252,224) (nearest outer cell of each ~60) ->yellow. Pull yellow upward around(260,168), then into sink(268,124). Re-evaluate centers/capture if exact-edge move fails.

[Before action · message]
The four magentas form two natural pairs. I’ll merge the left pair at the far-right feasible center (116,232), producing a purple already biased toward the middle.

[Before action · message]
The left pair produced a purple centered at (116,236). The right magentas are actually centered at (344,216) and (432,216); a midpoint pulse at (388,216) should merge them into the second purple.

[Before action · message]
The right magentas merged, but the upward-moving left pink hazard struck the stationary left purple during the long action: that purple is no longer at (116,236), and a magenta appeared near (136,160). I’ll map the final cells to see whether the purple split into two recoverable magentas or one was consumed.

[Before action · pixels]
At turn58 final, enumerate every tier-color connected component and light-pink component. Did the former left purple split into two magentas, and if so where are both?

[Before action · message]
The map shows only one magenta and one purple—half of the struck purple was consumed, so the yellow can no longer be built. I’ll undo the right merge, restoring the intact left purple and both right magentas, then move the vulnerable purple away before allowing another hazard advance.

[Before action · message]
Undo restored the intact purple at (116,236) and both right magentas. The left hazard is directly below it; I’ll immediately pull the purple up-right to (180,216), beyond the hazard’s rising path.

[Before action · message]
The hazard is tracking upward, so moving the purple upward kept it in the chase path. I’ll undo that dodge and instead pull the restored purple down-right, letting the rising hazard pass above it while I merge the right pair next.

[Before action · message]
The pre-dodge state is restored. I expect a pull to (172,268) to move the left purple below and right of the rising left hazard, so it will be safe during the following right-side merge.

[Before action · message]

GUIDE:
Core game model:
- ACTION6 emits a shrinking pulse. A normal/tier object relocates to the click-aligned grid position when a painted/occupied part is within roughly 60–64 px. Boundary behavior is inconsistent; use <=58 px to a cell/painted edge when possible. Large pieces can be selected far from their center via a near edge.
- Normal strict merges: exactly two same-tier pieces at one pulse upgrade cyan1 -> magenta2 -> purple3 -> yellow4 -> orange6; red7 is above orange. A lone piece relocates. Mixed captures can consume/corrupt one object, so explicitly exclude all unrelated pieces.
- Light-family glyph tiers use the same strict pairing: two light-pink arrow glyphs -> one green glyph; two green glyphs -> one dark-red glyph. Pink is slingshotted/phase-controlled by a pulse; merged green/dark glyphs relocate to the focus but drift several grid steps during later actions if not retained.
- Free (not pulse-controlled) pink contact downgrades a normal tier and knocks it away; pink survives/stops: red7 -> orange6; orange6 -> yellow4; purple -> magenta; magenta -> cyan. A pulse-controlled pink phases harmlessly through pieces. Set up contact/embedding, then use a pulse far from both to trigger damage. Natural pink trajectories can also cause intended hits.
- Header large glyphs are required deliveries. Blue disks are receivers; place target deeply in the blue footprint. Filled normal targets visibly remain. Sparse family glyphs often fail shallow placements; use a longer entry from outside to exact receiver center. Receivers appear role/position matched in multi-target levels (normal targets generally left; family glyph generally lower-right), but this remains partly uncertain.
- ACTION7 restores the previous actionable state. Bottom segmented bar is click budget.

- Proven second-family construction: four pinks can all be used even if one first hits red, since contact does not consume pink; pair them into two greens, then merge greens into dark red.
